lines.name: Concrete Saints
lines.style: Bold urban screen-print look mixing chunky woodcut-style illustration, prayer-candle and stained-glass parody art, subway-tile mosaic type, graffiti-era wildstyle and tag lettering, varsity block letters and hand-painted sign-shop scripts. Thick outlines, slight grit and halftone, nothing glossy. Dark-shirt palette: bone white #EDE6D6, safety orange #FF5F1F, subway green #3FA34D, signal yellow #F5C518, brick red #C8452E. Light-shirt palette: asphalt #2B2B2B, brick red #B23A26, subway green #2E7D3E, faded navy #23395B. Mood: proud, funny, a little gritty, very local.
lines.blurb: Concrete Saints is our love letter to the block: pigeons with halos, water towers, subway tile and the corner that raised you. Heavy tees, loud lettering and jokes only city people get. Tagline: "Blessed by the block."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\01 Urban Streetwear\Concrete Saints

lines.name: Deadstock Society
lines.style: Style H, modern streetwear brand graphic: extra-large back prints built on huge stacked heavy condensed sans-serif type, with the subject (generic high-tops and low-tops, shoeboxes, raffle tickets, countdown clocks, tissue paper; no real brand shapes, logos or stitching patterns) drawn as a bold cut-out silhouette that overlaps the letters. Hype-brand details fill the edges: thin rule lines, registration marks and a tiny barcode, never extra words. Strictly two inks per design. Dark shirts: sole off-white #F4F1EA plus one loud accent, usually box orange #F26B21, sometimes acid lime #C6F432 or icy blue #A8D8EA. Light shirts: midnight navy #1B2A41 plus box orange #D9531E. Mood: confident, graphic, collector-proud, funny in small print.
lines.blurb: Deadstock Society is for the people who set alarms for drops, keep every box and wince at a toe crease. Raffle losses, grail hunts and shoe-room pride, printed loud on heavy tees. Tagline: "Keep the box."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\01 Urban Streetwear\Deadstock Society

lines.name: Late Night Bodega
lines.niche: corner stores and late-night city food culture
lines.style: Style F, retro 1960s comic and bodega-flyer pop art: heavy halftone dot shading, bold outlines, motion lines and jagged comic-burst headlines, like a bootleg corner-store flyer crossed with a pulp comic panel. Subjects stay the bodega world: the unimpressed orange tabby mascot, chopped cheese, deli counters, neon window signs, heat lamps and milk crates. Lettering is chunky comic-book headline caps with drop shadows, pulp display serifs and punchy grocery-flyer brush script. Dark shirts use three inks: neon red #FF3B3B (or hot pink #FF6FB5), deli yellow #FFD23F and cream #F3E9D2. Light shirts use deep red #B3261E, mustard yellow #C9971C and navy #1F2A44. Mood: loud, cozy, after-hours, neighborhood-loyal.
lines.blurb: Late Night Bodega celebrates the corner store that never really closes: the cat on the chip rack, the chopped cheese at 2 a.m., the guy who knows your order. Neon signs, deli paper and inside jokes for night owls. Tagline: "The usual?"
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\01 Urban Streetwear\Late Night Bodega

lines.name: Maison Elevé
lines.niche: quiet luxury, resort and members-club style
lines.style: Style D, detailed vintage engraving with old-money romance: fine crosshatching and line shading on heraldic crests, interlocking monograms, laurel wreaths, rampant lions and swans, regatta pennants, luggage labels and resort-club badges, with small marks drawn to look like fine embroidery. Lettering is elegant high-contrast Didone serif caps, spaced engraved Roman small caps and flowing copperplate script. Two inks per design. Light shirts: deep navy #1F2A44 and antique gold #B08D57. Dark shirts: ivory cream #F3EBDD and champagne gold #D8BF8A. Mood: calm, polished, old-world with a wink.
lines.blurb: Maison Elevé is quiet luxury on a soft tee: monograms, crests, serif wordmarks and resort-club emblems that look like they came from a private clubhouse. Understated, a little witty, never loud. Tagline: "Quietly exceptional."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\02 Luxury\Maison Elevé

lines.name: Complication Club
lines.style: Style D, technical horological engraving: fine crosshatched etchings of generic movements, gear trains, balance wheels, tourbillon cages, dials and cases (no real brand dials, logos, crowns or signature hands), laid out like antique patent plates, watchmaker catalog pages and engraved emblems. Lettering is elegant high-contrast Didone serif caps, engraved serif caps with fine technical small caps and dial-style numerals, and a flowing copperplate script for asides. Two inks per design. Dark shirts: antique gold #C8A15A and cream #F2E8D5. Light shirts: deep navy #1C2B4A and antique brass #A67C3D. Mood: nerdy, precise, warmly self-aware.
lines.blurb: Complication Club is for the people who check wrists before faces and talk movements over dinner. Exploded calibers, lume shots, waitlist jokes and the eternal promise of one more watch. Tagline: "Wound tight, running well."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\02 Luxury\Complication Club

lines.name: Gilded Pour
lines.style: Style D, vintage spirits-label engraving: fine cross-hatched linework like a 19th-century distillery label, ornate filigree frames, crests, wax-seal badges, barrels, stills and cut-crystal glassware drawn with crisp highlights. Lettering mixes high-contrast Didone serifs, engraved small caps, condensed Victorian display type and flowing copperplate script. Dark shirts use two inks: antique gold #C8952E and warm cream #F1E4C8. Light shirts use three: oxblood #6B1E2A, charred oak brown #2B1D14 and antique gold #A9781F. Mood: warm, unhurried, a little smug, like the last pour of the night by a fireplace.
lines.blurb: Gilded Pour is for the people who own more glencairns than coffee mugs, know their mash bill by heart and will absolutely add a few drops of water, thank you. Gold-leaf crests, rickhouse engravings and home-bar inside jokes, pressed to order on soft, heavyweight tees. Tagline: "Drink the good stuff. Wear it too."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\02 Luxury\Gilded Pour

lines.name: Route & Rust
lines.style: Faded 1970s roadside-souvenir tees: the kind of gas-station, diner and county-fair shirt you find soft and cracked at an estate sale. Every piece sits on retro sunset stripes, a faded rainbow arc or a small sunburst, with simple flat illustration, chunky rounded 70s lettering with a drop shadow and the odd brush-script line, all under a heavily distressed cracked-ink texture. Faded, muted palette: Faded Cream #EADCB8, Mustard #C99A2E, Burnt Orange #C0612B, Dusty Teal #5E8C84 and Faded Brown #5A3B2A; cream, mustard, orange and teal carry the dark shirts, brown, rust, mustard and teal carry the light ones. Best on washed blanks like Ivory, Bay, Sandstone, Butter and Pepper. Mood: warm, sun-bleached small-town pride.
lines.blurb: Route & Rust is the glovebox full of old road maps: gas-station badges, diner signs, county-fair posters and hand-painted roadside lettering from the 1950s to the 70s. Every design looks like it has been through a few hundred summers, in the best way. Tagline: "Built for the long way home."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\03 Vintage Americana\Route and Rust

lines.name: Vinyl Hours
lines.style: Faded 1970s record-sleeve and record-store tees: the shirt you'd have bought at the counter of an independent shop in 1976 and worn soft ever since. Groove circles, center labels, turntables and crate-digging scenes in simple flat illustration, set on retro sunset stripes, rainbow arcs or small sunbursts, with chunky rounded 70s lettering with a drop shadow, groovy brush script and a heavily distressed cracked-ink texture. Faded, muted palette: Sleeve Cream #EADFC6, Hi-Fi Mustard #CFA03C, Burnt Orange #C9622B, Faded Teal #4F8682 and Groove Brown #3A2A20; cream, mustard, orange and teal carry the dark shirts, brown, orange, teal and mustard carry the light ones. Mood: warm, nerdy, unhurried, like the last hour before the record shop closes.
lines.blurb: Vinyl Hours is for people who lose whole Saturdays in the dollar bin and still flip every record over for the B-side. Old label graphics, hi-fi ad parodies and crate-digger jokes, made to order for the listening room. Tagline: "Drop the needle. Stay a while."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\03 Vintage Americana\Vinyl Hours

lines.name: Neon Motor Court
lines.niche: road trips and vintage motel culture
lines.style: Faded 1970s motel-souvenir tees with a neon accent: the gift-shop shirt from a motor court off the old highway, washed a hundred times. Motel signs, kidney pools, key fobs, station wagons and desert roads in simple flat illustration over retro sunset stripes, rainbow arcs or small sunbursts, with chunky rounded 70s lettering with a drop shadow, 70s neon-tube script, and a heavily distressed cracked-ink texture; one thin neon-pink glow accent per design keeps the buzz of the sign. Faded, muted palette: Postcard Cream #EDE0C4, Sodium Mustard #D6A73E, Dusty Turquoise #5FA9A4 and Faded Navy #2F3B55 with a Neon Pink #FF5FA2 accent; cream, mustard and turquoise carry the dark shirts, navy, rust red and dusty teal carry the light ones. Mood: warm night air, buzzing signs, windows down.
lines.blurb: Neon Motor Court is for people who pull off the highway for a good sign, not a good review. Buzzing vacancy neon, kidney-shaped pools, diamond key fobs and postcards from places you only meant to drive through. Tagline: "Pull in. Stay late."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\03 Vintage Americana\Neon Motor Court

lines.name: Dial-Up Days
lines.style: Y2K liquid chrome: late-90s desktop nostalgia rendered as glossy 3D chrome. Modems, flip phones, CRTs, discs, pagers and pixel cursors float among sparkles and star glints, with shiny liquid-chrome bubble lettering, chrome glitter script and small glossy pixel type, all built from iridescent galactic metallic gradients and printed as crisp spot colors. Palette: Chrome Silver #D9DEE6, Iridescent Baby Blue #8FD3FF, Bubblegum Pink #FF8AD8 and Electric Violet #6B3FD4 for the dark shirts; Gunmetal Chrome #4A5060, Cobalt #1E3AA8, Hot Magenta #D6338A and Electric Violet for the light ones. Mood: glossy, playful, a little glitchy, totally sincere.
lines.blurb: Dial-Up Days is the screech of a modem, an away message you rewrote nine times and a phone you could snap shut when you were mad. Chrome bubble type, pixel cursors, glitter text and CRT glow for anyone who grew up waiting for a page to load. Tagline: "Still connecting."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\04 Y2K and Retro Tech\Dial-Up Days

lines.name: Save Point Society
lines.style: Chrome arcade marquee meets chunky pixel art: every piece pairs 8-bit and 16-bit sprites with visible square pixels and shiny Y2K liquid-chrome marquee lettering, sparkles, star glints and iridescent metallic gradients, with small chunky pixel type for second lines. Dark-shirt palette: Chrome Silver #D9DEE6, Power-Up Cyan #3CD3E8, Coin Gold #F7C548 and Hit-Point Red #E8434F. Light-shirt palette: Gunmetal Chrome #4A5060, Deep Plum #4A2A5E, Console Teal #1E7A80 and Brick Red #B23A3A. Mood: nostalgic, playful and a little smug about owning the original hardware.
lines.blurb: Save Point Society is for anyone who learned patience by blowing on a cartridge and praying. Pixel art, arcade glow and couch co-op jokes, pressed on heavyweight tees for players who still keep their save files sacred. Tagline: "Progress saved. Life continues."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\04 Y2K and Retro Tech\Save Point Society

lines.name: Low Battery Social
lines.style: MIDImalism for the chronically online: minimalist single continuous fine-line icons (batteries, chat bubbles, typing dots, envelopes, read receipts, loading rings, charger cables) with lots of negative space and small spaced-out sans-serif caps, the occasional thin script or light serif. Recurring character: Lo, a sleepy little line-drawn battery. One main ink plus one bold accent used on a single detail. Dark shirts: Bone White #EFE9DC with Low-Battery Red #EE3B2E. Light shirts: Ink Navy #1F2A44 with Battery Red #C7362B. Mood: tired, petty, quietly proud of surviving another Monday.
lines.blurb: Low Battery Social is a club for everyone running on 1% and a cold coffee: read receipts off, camera off, out of office in spirit. Lo, our tired little battery, keeps the faith for the inbox-weary. Tagline: "Running on 1%. Still showing up."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\04 Y2K and Retro Tech\Low Battery Social

lines.name: Trailhead Standard
lines.style: Faded 1970s park-souvenir and camp-poster tees: flat layered mountains, pines, lakes and campfires set against retro sunset rainbow stripes, arrowhead and round badge frames, and a heavily distressed, cracked-ink texture like a tee that has been through fifty summers of camp. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s type with a drop shadow, with the odd retro 70s script accent. Dark-shirt palette (muted, light inks): Faded Cream #EFE3C8, Mustard #D4A23C, Burnt Orange #C8642F and Dusty Sage #9BAF8A. Light-shirt palette (deep inks): Faded Forest Green #3E5643, Rust #A5502D, Mustard #B98A2A and Brown #5A3E2B. Best on garment-dyed washed blanks. Mood: calm, sturdy and nostalgic, like a well-worn trail map from the glovebox.
lines.blurb: Trailhead Standard is our outdoor line: park-style badges, topo lines, campfires and trail maps for people who feel better with dirt on their boots. Every design looks like it came off a ranger-station postcard rack, minus the gift-shop markup. Tagline: "Outside is the standard."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\05 Outdoor Adventure\Trailhead Standard

lines.name: Summit Fever
lines.style: Faded 1970s sunset-stripe mountain tees: chunky mountains, cartoon hikers, boots, trekking poles, elevation profiles and summit flags set against a retro sunset of rainbow stripes, with a heavily distressed, cracked-ink texture like a thrifted souvenir tee. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s type with a drop shadow, with a retro 70s script for punchlines. Light-shirt palette (deep, faded inks): Faded Brown #5B3F2C, Burnt Orange #C8642F, Mustard #C99A2E and Dusty Teal #3F7E7A. Dark-shirt palette (muted, light inks): Faded Cream #EFE3C8, Mustard #D4A23C, Burnt Orange #D9733A and Dusty Teal #8FB8B0. Best on washed blanks like Ivory, Bay, Sandstone, Butter and Granite. Mood: sweaty, sunburnt, self-aware and very happy to be up here.
lines.blurb: Summit Fever is for hikers who know the false summit is coming and climb anyway. Switchbacks, blisters, trail names and the sacred bag of trail mix, drawn by people who count elevation gain for fun. Tagline: "No known cure. Just more peaks."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\05 Outdoor Adventure\Summit Fever

lines.name: Night Sky Survey
lines.style: Antique star-atlas engraving: highly detailed etched illustrations with fine crosshatching, stippled starfields, dotted constellation lines, brass telescopes, crescent moons, orbit rings and observatory domes, framed like plates from an old celestial atlas. Lettering is elegant high-contrast serif, engraved serif capitals and the occasional copperplate script. Two inks only. Dark shirts: Starlight Cream #F3EBD3 and Antique Gold #C9A24A. Light shirts: Midnight Navy #1B2340 and Antique Gold #A57C1B. Mood: quiet wonder with a nerdy wink, like a page torn from an 1800s observatory folio.
lines.blurb: Night Sky Survey is for backyard astronomers, star-party regulars and anyone who has driven two hours for darker skies. Moon phases, red flashlights and the eternal new-telescope cloud curse, drawn like pages from an old star atlas. Tagline: "Clear skies, always."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\05 Outdoor Adventure\Night Sky Survey

lines.name: Quiet Form
lines.niche: minimalist design and line art lovers
lines.style: Pure minimal line art: single continuous fine-line drawings with an even pen weight, simple geometric shapes (circles, arches, horizon lines, grids) and small spaced-out sans-serif caps or a light high-contrast serif, set in generous negative space. One ink per design, sometimes with a single small accent color on one detail. Light-shirt inks: Charcoal #2B2B2B, Ink Navy #1F2A44, Sage #6F7F5E, with Terracotta #B5543A as the accent. Dark-shirt inks: Bone #EDE6D6 and Sand #D9C3A0, with Sage Mist #B7C4A8 or Clay #D98B6C as the accent. Mood: calm, airy, gallery-wall restraint.
lines.blurb: Quiet Form is our minimalist line: single-line drawings, small type and a lot of empty space. Two inks at most, nothing shouting, everything placed on purpose. Tagline: "Say less. Mean it."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\06 Minimalist\Quiet Form

lines.name: Holy Grounds
lines.style: Minimal line art with one warm coffee accent (MIDImalism): every design is a single continuous fine-line drawing of one coffee object or the bean mascot, with lots of negative space and the parody format (prayer card, varsity lockup, street sign, seal, belt) reduced to a few thin outline strokes. Lettering is small, spaced-out sans-serif caps, sometimes paired with one word in a thin high-contrast serif. One line ink plus a single accent fill on one small element (the crema, a drop, a halo). Recurring world: Beanie the coffee-bean mascot, gooseneck kettle, portafilter and tamper, burr grinder, pour-over cone, moka pot, scale and timer, rosetta latte art, coffee cherries. Dark-shirt inks: crema cream #F2E3C6 line with a burnt copper #D9773B accent. Light-shirt inks: roast brown #4A2C1D line with a burnt copper #B5562A accent. Mood: quiet, devout, caffeinated, a little smug about grind size.
lines.blurb: Holy Grounds treats the morning cup like a sacrament: gooseneck kettles, blooming pour-overs, tamped pucks and latte art that was supposed to be a swan. Loud, clean tees for people who own a scale just for beans. Tagline: "Blessed be the bloom."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\06 Minimalist\Holy Grounds

lines.name: Plant Parent Co.
lines.style: Loose botanical watercolor and ink: expressive, quick-brush paintings of leaves, vines, pots and propagation jars with soft wet-in-wet washes, small splashes and drips, held together by a light, confident ink outline so each plant still reads at a glance. Lettering is hand-lettered brush script for the main words with small brush-written caps for the second line. Soft, muted, earthy color with plenty of breathing room. Light-shirt inks: Deep Leaf Green (#2F4A32), Terracotta (#B65E3C), Soil Brown (#4A3426), Sage Moss (#6E7F45). Dark-shirt inks: Mint Leaf (#A8D5B0), Clay Pink (#E3A58A), Cream (#F2EBDA), Soft Lime (#C7D96B). Mood: fresh, gentle, a little self-aware.
lines.blurb: Plant Parent Co. is for people with more pots than chairs. Clean botanical line drawings, small type and the jokes you only get after your first case of root rot. Tagline: "Bright, indirect, and doing our best."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\06 Minimalist\Plant Parent Co

lines.name: Dust & Spur
lines.style: Faded 1970s rodeo-poster and desert-souvenir tees: flat retro illustration of riders, broncs, saguaros, longhorn skulls and mesas, often set against a striped sunset or a sliced desert sun with retro rainbow bands, finished with a heavily distressed, worn cracked-ink texture so every print looks like a thrifted gas-station souvenir. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s type with a drop shadow, faded Tuscan rodeo-poster letters and a looping 70s rope script, set in arches, banners and stacked lines. Light-shirt inks (faded, muted): Saddle Brown (#5A3A22), Faded Rust (#A8452A), Dusty Turquoise (#2E7F7A), Faded Mustard (#B88A26). Dark-shirt inks: Faded Bone (#E6DCC3), Sunset Orange (#D9803F), Dusty Turquoise (#6FB7AE), Mustard Gold (#D6AE52). Mood: dusty, warm, sunburnt and a little rowdy.
lines.blurb: Dust & Spur is our Western line: desert sunsets, saguaros, horseshoes and rodeo-poster lettering, printed the way an old feed-store sign fades. Made for boots, open roads and long evenings outside. Tagline: "Ride slow. Kick dust."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\07 Western\Dust and Spur

lines.name: Two Step Social
lines.niche: country music fans and line dancers
lines.style: Faded 1970s honky-tonk and dance-hall poster tees: flat retro illustration of boots, hats, jukeboxes, marquees and dance floors, often over retro sunset stripes or a sunburst, with a heavily distressed, worn cracked-ink texture like a decades-old bar-giveaway shirt. Neon signs appear as subjects but are drawn in the same sun-faded flat inks, never glowing. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s type with a drop shadow, a looping 70s script, faded Western slab letters and Tuscan dance-hall poster type. Dark-shirt inks (faded): Faded Cream (#EADFC6), Dusty Rose (#D98A9E), Faded Turquoise (#6DB9B0), Mustard Gold (#D9A94A). Light-shirt inks: Deep Rose (#A23E5A), Faded Teal (#2F716C), Saddle Brown (#4A2E1F), Gold Ochre (#A9822F). Mood: Saturday night, sawdust floors, loud jukebox, big grins.
lines.blurb: Two Step Social is for dance-hall regulars, line-dance crews and anyone who knows the count is quick, quick, slow, slow. Neon honky-tonk signs, jukeboxes, boots and disco-ball cowboy hats. Tagline: "See you on the dance floor."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\07 Western\Two Step Social

lines.name: Ranch Hand Supply
lines.style: Detailed vintage feed-store engraving: horses, cattle, barn cats, ranch dogs, hay bales, tack and tools drawn as fine etchings with crosshatched shading, like plates from an old ranch-supply catalog or livestock auction bill. Layouts borrow feed-sack labels, rope-twist frames, ribbon banners, medicine-tin labels and branding-iron badges. Lettering is elegant high-contrast serif caps, engraved Western slab caps, small tracked serif caps and an engraved copperplate script. Two inks per design. Light-shirt inks: Saddle Brown #5A3A22, Barn Red #8E2B1F. Dark-shirt inks: Cream #EFE3C8, Antique Gold #C9A24A. Mood: early mornings, honest work, dry humor and a little dust on everything.
lines.blurb: Ranch Hand Supply is for the people who feed before they eat: barn chores, hay season, feed-store runs and horses that cost more than the truck. Every design reads like something you would find tacked up in an old tack room, with the jokes only horse people get. Tagline: "Up before the rooster."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\07 Western\Ranch Hand Supply

lines.name: Salt & Wheels
lines.style: Faded 1970s surf-shop souvenir tees: retro striped sunsets and rainbow stripe bands, curling waves, palm trees, old-school boards, beach vans and cartoon sharks, drawn as flat bold shapes with a heavily distressed, cracked-ink texture so every print looks like it survived twenty summers in a beach-shop window. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s type with a drop shadow, fat groovy display letters with stripe shadows, retro bubble script and small rounded caps. Inks are faded and muted. Dark-shirt inks: Faded Cream #EFE3C8, Mustard #D9A93F, Burnt Orange #C8642B, Faded Teal #5E9C98. Light-shirt inks: Chocolate Brown #5A3B28, Burnt Orange #B9541F, Mustard #B88A22, Dusty Teal #3D7774. Best on washed blanks like Ivory, Butter, Bay, Sandstone and Pepper. Mood: warm, sun-bleached, loose and nostalgic.
lines.blurb: Salt & Wheels is our skate and surf line, pulled straight from 1970s to 90s surf-shop walls and skate-deck art: striped sunsets, palm trees, checkerboard and fat outlined type. It is for anyone who splits the day between the break and the bowl. Tagline: "Sun's out, wheels down."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\08 Skate and Surf\Salt and Wheels

lines.name: Grip Tape Gospel
lines.style: American traditional tattoo flash applied to skateboarding: decks, trucks, wheels, bearings, curbs, handrails, halos, swallows, roses, stars and ribbon banners, drawn with thick bold outlines and flat solid color fills like a sheet of flash on a tattoo-shop wall, with a wink at the brand's gospel theme (halos, rays, devotional cards). Lettering is bold tattoo-flash block letters, chunky banner lettering, classic tattoo script and tattoo-style blackletter. Dark-shirt inks: Cream #F1E6CC (outlines), Tattoo Red #D23A2A, Mustard Yellow #E3B23C, Jade Green #3E9B6E. Light-shirt inks: Ink Black #1E1E1E (outlines), Tattoo Red #C4301F, Mustard Yellow #C99A22, Jade Green #2E7D55. Mood: scrappy, funny, loud and proud of every scar.
lines.blurb: Grip Tape Gospel is for skaters who measure a good day in bruises and landed tricks. Ollies, bails, bearings, security guards and one more try: the whole sermon, preached from the curb. Tagline: "Fall. Get up. Push."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\08 Skate and Surf\Grip Tape Gospel

lines.name: Dawn Patrol Surf Club
lines.style: Faded 1970s surf-club tees: layered sunset stripe bands behind peeling waves, longboards, pelicans, lighthouses, tide charts, wood-paneled wagons and sleepy surfers with coffee, drawn as flat retro shapes with a distressed, cracked-ink texture like a club shirt that has been to a thousand dawn sessions. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s surf letters with drop shadows, soft rounded display type with sunset-stripe shadows, loose surf-shop script and small rounded caps. Dark-shirt inks: Shell Cream #F2E6CF, Sunset Peach #EDA77E, Faded Coral #D9705A, Seafoam #8CC7B5. Light-shirt inks: Faded Navy #2C4A63, Sunset Coral #C8553F, Mustard Gold #B98A2A, Sea Teal #3E7B76. Best on washed blanks like Bay, Ivory, Sandstone, Chalky Mint and Pepper. Mood: calm, salty, quietly proud and a little sleepy.
lines.blurb: Dawn Patrol Surf Club is for surfers who check the forecast before the weather, wax up in the dark and paddle out while the town is still asleep. Glassy mornings, tide charts, longboards and cold-water hoods, with the lineup jokes only surfers get. Tagline: "Paddle out before the world wakes up."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\08 Skate and Surf\Dawn Patrol Surf Club

lines.name: Nocturne
lines.style: Gothic vintage engraving: moths, ravens, crows, bats, skulls crowned with flowers, candles, hourglasses, keys and tarot-card frames rendered like plates from an antique naturalist's book or a Victorian mourning card, with fine crosshatching, stippled shading and ornate engraved borders. Lettering is ornate gothic blackletter, elegant high-contrast serif caps, small tracked engraved caps and thin copperplate script. Two-to-three-ink restraint: Dark-shirt inks: Bone Cream #E8DFCC, Antique Gold #C9A55A, Dusty Rose #C98B8F (accent). Light-shirt inks: Ink Black #1C1A1F, Oxblood #6E1E24, Antique Brass #8C6A2F (accent). Mood: moody, romantic, a little wry, never gory.
lines.blurb: Nocturne is our dark gothic line: moths, ravens, skulls in bloom, moon phases and tarot frames, drawn like pages from an old engraving book. It is for night owls, black-wardrobe loyalists and anyone who finds the creepy stuff beautiful. Tagline: "Beautiful things come out at night."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\09 Dark and Gothic\Nocturne

lines.name: Midnight Apothecary
lines.style: Antique apothecary-label engraving: corked bottles, tins, mortar and pestle, herb sprigs, moths, moons, crystals and tarot-card frames drawn like 19th-century pharmacy labels and botanical plates, with fine crosshatching, stipple shading, ornate engraved frames, ribbons and corner flourishes. Lettering is ornate engraved Victorian serif caps, elegant high-contrast serif, small tracked engraved caps and fine copperplate script. Dark-shirt inks: Bone Cream #EDE6D6, Antique Gold #C9A44C, Sage Green #9CAF88. Light-shirt inks: Deep Plum #3E2A47, Forest Green #2F4A3A, Antique Brass #A8842F. Mood: candlelit, mysterious and a little bit funny, never scary or religious.
lines.blurb: Midnight Apothecary is a shop for kitchen witches, tarot readers and anyone with a windowsill full of crystals and drying herbs. Every shirt reads like a label from a candlelit back-room apothecary, made for people who brew moon water and laugh about it too. Tagline: "Remedies & rituals, after dark."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\09 Dark and Gothic\Midnight Apothecary

lines.name: Dead Letter Book Club
lines.style: Retro 1960s pulp-horror paperback covers and horror-comic panels: dramatic cover-art illustration with bold ink outlines, heavy halftone dots, comic motion lines and burst shapes, lurid moonlight and candle glow. Recurring world: the Night Librarian (a skeleton in cat-eye glasses with a candle), ravens, towering TBR stacks, coffin bookshelves, moths, overdue stamps, haunted stacks and graveyards. Lettering is pulp-paperback title type: dripping and jagged horror letters, slanted condensed titles, comic block letters with halftone drop shadows and comic burst headlines. Dark-shirt palette: paperback cream #F1E4C6, blood red #D2302C, pulp yellow #F2C12E, spectral blue #5AA9D6. Light-shirt palette: midnight navy #1F2340, blood red #B3221E, mustard #C8921E, deep teal blue #1F5F8B. Mood: spooky, campy, cozy and smug about reading.
lines.blurb: Dead Letter Book Club is for the people reading horror by candlelight at 3 a.m.: the Night Librarian, ravens on the shelf, overdue stamps and a TBR pile that could crush a man. Heavy tees, spooky lettering and jokes every bookish goth already lives. Tagline: "Read in the dark."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\09 Dark and Gothic\Dead Letter Book Club

lines.name: Varsity Archive
lines.niche: retro sports and vintage athletic style
lines.style: Faded 1970s vintage athletic-department tees, like a gym shirt that has been through a hundred washes: chunky rounded 70s varsity and collegiate letters with drop shadows, loose swash scripts with tails, felt-pennant shapes, trophy and laurel emblems, small retro stripe accents and simple single-figure athlete illustrations, all with a heavily distressed, cracked-ink texture. Inks are faded and muted. Light-shirt inks: faded varsity navy (#3A4A66), washed red (#A8564B), mustard gold (#C79A4A) and pine green (#557060). Dark-shirt inks: bleacher cream (#E6DAC0), mustard gold (#D2A55A), washed red (#C46A5C) and dusty sky blue (#94AFC4). Best on washed blanks like Ivory, Bay, Sandstone, Butter, Granite and Pepper. Warm, nostalgic and sporty, with no real teams, leagues, schools or logos.
lines.blurb: Varsity Archive is our retro sports line: shirts that look like they were pulled from a 1970s athletic-department storeroom. Varsity arches, pennants, trophies and every sport from track to bowling night, with no teams attached, just the feeling of game day. Tagline: "Pulled from the equipment room."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\10 Retro Sports\Varsity Archive

lines.name: Fifth Quarter Tailgate
lines.style: Faded 1970s game-day bootleg tees, the kind sold out of a trunk in the stadium lot and worn soft for decades: cartoon grills, coolers, folding chairs, station wagons, pennants and stadium lights with thick outlines, retro stripe accents and starbursts, under a heavily distressed, cracked-ink texture. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s varsity type, slab-serif headers and swash script, all with drop shadows. Inks are faded and muted. Light-shirt inks: stadium green (#4E6B4F), washed brick red (#A35147), faded navy (#3B4760) and mustard (#C99A3E). Dark-shirt inks: bleacher cream (#E8DCC3), mustard (#D6A64C), washed tomato red (#CF6A55) and sage field green (#93AE7E). Best on washed blanks like Ivory, Sandstone, Butter, Bay, Granite and Pepper. Loud, friendly and game-day happy, with no real schools, teams, mascots or logos.
lines.blurb: Fifth Quarter Tailgate is for the people who get to the lot at 7 a.m. for a noon kickoff. Grills, coolers, folding chairs and queso, drawn like an old game-day program, with no team names so everyone can wear them. Tagline: "The game ends. The tailgate doesn't."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\10 Retro Sports\Fifth Quarter Tailgate

lines.name: Bogey Bandits
lines.style: Faded 1970s country-club souvenir tees, like a pro-shop shirt found in a thrift store: simple cartoon golfers, golf balls with faces, flagsticks, carts, clubs and fairway scenes, clubhouse badges and crests, retro sunset-stripe accents, all under a heavily distressed, cracked-ink texture. Lettering is chunky rounded 70s serifs, collegiate block letters and loopy 70s script, with drop shadows. Inks are faded and muted. Light-shirt inks: fairway green (#4F6E52), washed navy (#3D4A63), faded flag red (#B05A4C) and sand tan (#B99A68). Dark-shirt inks: clubhouse cream (#E9DFC6), sage grass green (#9BB88C), washed flag red (#D06E5E) and sand gold (#D9B977). Best on washed blanks like Ivory, Sandstone, Butter, Bay, Chalky Mint and Pepper. Easygoing, sunny and self-deprecating, with no real courses, tournaments, brands or players.
lines.blurb: Bogey Bandits is for weekend golfers who keep score loosely and laugh about it. Mulligans, sand traps, lost balls and the 19th hole, drawn in a retro country-club style that looks good at the course and the clubhouse bar. Tagline: "Steal a few strokes."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\12 Series 2\10 Retro Sports\Bogey Bandits

lines.name: Side Quest Supply
lines.niche: teens and gen z: gaming, anime-style art, skate and school-life irony
lines.style: Gen Z streetwear that looks like an open-world game menu: glossy Y2K chrome and inflated puff-print bubble type, glitchy RGB-split pixel fonts, original anime and manga-style teen characters with speed lines, and a recurring cast of icons: Blip (a round squishy pixel slime with star-shaped eyes), a glowing yellow diamond quest marker, pixel hearts, loading bars, stars and butterflies. Oversized back hits, mostly lowercase slogans. Dark-shirt palette (pastel and neon on black): bubblegum pink #FF8AD8, cyber lime #B6FF3B, ice blue #8FE3FF, lilac #C9A7FF, chrome silver #D9DDE3. Light-shirt palette (earth tones on cream): coffee brown #4A3426, rust orange #A8502E, moss green #5C6B3C, faded denim blue #3E5675. Mood: ironic, cute, a little chaotic, always PG.
lines.blurb: Side Quest Supply treats regular teen life like an open-world game: homework is a boss fight, snacks are a save point and every detour counts as a quest. Blip the pixel slime, chrome bubble type, butterflies and anime-style skaters show up all over the drop. Tagline: "Every detour counts."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\13 Series 3\01 Teen Streetwear\Side Quest Supply

lines.name: Velvet Static
lines.niche: designer streetwear drops, fit culture and heavyweight blanks
lines.style: Designer-drop look built on sharp gothic blackletter, high-contrast didone fashion serifs and widely spaced sans capitals, finished with liquid-chrome airbrush, rhinestone-dot texture, fine engraved linework and distressed vintage-wash grain. Recurring house icons: the Static Angel (a classical stone angel whose halo is a ring of TV static), the Wire Rose (a rose bound in barbed wire), a jeweled crown, flames and a winged vintage television. Mostly one to three inks per piece, often tonal. Dark-shirt palette: bone cream #EFE6D2, chrome silver #C9CCD1, antique gold #C9A45C, dusty rose #D8A7A9, pale ice blue #BFD9E6. Light-shirt palette: espresso brown #3B2A22, oxblood red #6E1A24, gunmetal grey #3A3D42, aged bronze #7A5C2E. Mood: expensive, cinematic, serious, never jokey.
lines.blurb: Velvet Static is a fictional fashion house built on noise and silk: angels with halos of TV static, roses bound in barbed wire, crowns, flames and blackletter wordmarks that look like the drop you waited in line for. Heavy tees, tonal inks, quiet on the front and loud on the back. Tagline: "Made loud. Worn quiet."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\13 Series 3\02 Luxury Streetwear\Velvet Static

lines.name: Cold Start Society
lines.niche: car enthusiasts: tuners, muscle car fans, track-day drivers and project-car builders
lines.style: Retro 80s and 90s motorsport and garage graphics: bold cartoon linework with halftone shading, rally livery stripes, racing-number roundels, speed lines, tachometer gauges, exploded-diagram line art and Japanese movie-poster layouts, always with generic unbranded cars (no logos, badges or real models). Recurring world: the turbo snail mascot (a snail whose shell is a turbocharger, in helmet and goggles), the frosted ignition key, the redline tach and the home garage. Lettering: extended racing italics, chrome-outlined poster type, stencil and hand-painted sign letters. Dark-shirt palette: cream #F2E8D5, rally orange #FF6B1A, signal yellow #FFC72C, racing teal #1FA6A0, redline red #E23B2E. Light-shirt palette: garage charcoal #2A2A2A, rally red #C8341F, deep teal #136F6B, navy #1E2F4F. Mood: nostalgic, funny, grease-under-the-nails proud.
lines.blurb: Cold Start Society is for everyone who lets it warm up first: tuners, muscle heads, track rats and the guy with three project cars in the yard. Rally stripes, tachometers, parts-store receipts and a turbo snail mascot who is late to everything except the pull. Tagline: "Let it warm up."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\13 Series 3\03 Car Culture\Cold Start Society

lines.name: Brass & Powder Co.
lines.niche: range shooters, reloaders, hunters and Second Amendment supporters
lines.style: Vintage sporting-goods and patriotic Americana: engraved antique ammo-box label layouts, distressed waving flags, cartridge cutaway diagrams, target rings, woodcut hunting-camp scenes and military stencil type. Firearms always appear generic and unbranded with no logos or markings, shown as objects on benches, racks or crossed in emblems, never aimed at anyone. Recurring world: the range officer eagle mascot (a bald eagle in hearing protection and yellow shooting glasses), rows of brass cartridges, the bullseye target and the house label "Brass & Powder Co.". Lettering: engraved serif capitals, slab-serif wood type, military stencil and retro script. Dark-shirt palette: brass gold #D4A84B, cream #EFE6D2, flag red #C8372D, faded blue #6F8FB5, safety orange #F26B21. Light-shirt palette: navy #1F2E4A, oxblood red #8E2A22, olive drab #4B5320, charcoal #2B2B2B. Mood: proud, old-school, funny and responsible.
lines.blurb: Brass & Powder Co. is for people who spend Saturdays at the range and weeknights at the reloading bench. Vintage ammo-box labels, distressed flags, deer camp and a range officer eagle who never forgets his eyes and ears. Proud, funny and always safe on the line. Tagline: "Eyes and ears. Always."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\13 Series 3\04 Guns and Ammo\Brass and Powder Co

lines.name: Box Season Customs
lines.niche: owners and fans of 70s-80s full-size box body sedans and Southern custom car culture
lines.style: 90s Southern airbrush tee meets car-show flyer: glossy chrome bubble letters, candy-paint gradients with drips, metal-flake sparkle and thin pinstripe swirls, prayer-candle and trophy parody art, all built around one recurring hero, a generic unbranded boxy 80s full-size sedan sitting high on oversized chrome rims (no badges, no grille logos), plus palmettos, Spanish moss oaks and Lowcountry sunsets. Thick outlines, soft airbrush glow, neon-on-black energy. Dark-shirt palette: candy apple red #E0262F, chrome silver #C9D1D9, candy tangerine #FF8A1F, lime flake green #7CFF4F, airbrush sky blue #3FC5F0. Light-shirt palette: deep candy red #A3161F, grape candy purple #3B1F5C, gunmetal #2E3338, palmetto green #1F5130. Mood: proud, loud, funny, show-ready.
lines.blurb: Box Season Customs is for the ones who sit high on purpose: big rims, candy paint thirteen coats deep, trunk rattling through the Lowcountry. Car-show trophies, Sunday detail service and every joke about rims costing more than the car. Tagline: "It's always box season."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\13 Series 3\05 Box Body Cars\Box Season Customs

lines.name: Square Body Social
lines.niche: owners and fans of 1973-1987 square body pickups
lines.style: Vintage 70s Americana truck graphics: faded rainbow sunset stripes, retro dealership-sign and road-trip badge layouts, blueprint side profiles, barn and field scenes, wood-grain panels and two-tone paint, all built around one recurring hero, a generic unbranded 1970s-80s square-body pickup with no badges or emblems, plus a loyal hound riding in the bed and a rusty parts truck in the weeds. Slightly worn print texture, clean bold outlines, retro script and chunky 70s serif lettering. Dark-shirt palette: cream #F1E6CF, harvest gold #E8B04A, burnt orange #E0702F, faded teal #7FB5A8, sunset red #D2492A. Light-shirt palette: rust brown #7A3B1E, deep teal #1E4D4A, faded navy #23395B, barn red #8E2A1F. Mood: warm, nostalgic, proud, a little rusty and very funny.
lines.blurb: Square Body Social is for the 73-87 crowd: restorers, farm-truck lifers, slammed and lifted builds, and every dad and kid with a project in the garage. Faded sunset stripes, a parts truck in the weeds and a bed dog who never misses a ride. Tagline: "Still square. Still running."
lines.folder: Business Plan and Ideas\13 Series 3\06 Square Body Trucks\Square Body Social

**What you get**
